import sys

def find_l_r(n, a, b_prime):
    l, r = -10**9, 10**9
    
    for i in range(4, n):
        if b_prime[i] == '1' and b_prime[i-1] == b_prime[i-2] == b_prime[i-3] == b_prime[i-4] == '0':
            l = max(l, max(a[i], a[i-1], a[i-2], a[i-3], a[i-4]) + 1)
        elif b_prime[i] == '0' and b_prime[i-1] == b_prime[i-2] == b_prime[i-3] == b_prime[i-4] == '1':
            r = min(r, min(a[i], a[i-1], a[i-2], a[i-3], a[i-4]))
    
    return l, r

input = sys.stdin.read
data = input().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = list(map(int, data[1:n+1]))
b_prime = data[n+1]

l, r = find_l_r(n, a, b_prime)
print(l, r)

The first line of input contains a single integer n (5 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) — the length of a and b'.
